reasons.plausibility: Interstitial carbon in BCC refractory alloys typically increases strength and reduces ductility by pinning dislocations, so the proposed mechanism of lowering lattice friction and enhancing dislocation mobility contradicts well-established behavior.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with specific measurements and a well-defined falsification criterion based on comparing ductility, high-temperature strength, and irradiation defect density.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is based on a physically incorrect mechanism; testing it would waste resources and not advance understanding of ductility improvement in this alloy.
